# DCGM Exporter Metrics and Deployment Authoring Contract

> Authoring contract, not a repository map: the verified rules for writing
> DCGM Exporter metric CSVs, CLI and environment settings, Helm values, and
> deployment examples. Agent working rules live in `AGENTS.md`.

This file is for LLMs and agents generating or modifying DCGM Exporter metrics,
configuration, deployment examples, and validation plans. Current repository
code and checked-in artifacts are the mechanical source of truth for behavior.
The official DCGM Exporter guide is authoritative for user-guide prose, and
the official DCGM field reference is authoritative for field semantics.

Do not invent flags, environment variables, metric labels, DCGM field names,
exporter-owned counter names, Helm values, or package behavior. If required
facts are not present in this repository, mark them unknown and ask for source
material.

## Source Of Truth And Validation Workflow

Use this order:

1. `pkg/cmd/app.go` defines CLI flags, environment variables, startup
   behavior, web config, pprof, logging, and runtime reload wiring.
   `internal/pkg/appconfig` defines the defaults (`DefaultConfig`), the flag-name
   strings, and the checks on configuration values.
2. `internal/pkg/counters/const.go` and `internal/pkg/counters/exporter_counters.go`
   define exporter-owned metric names.
3. `etc/default-counters.csv` defines the default shipped metric list, and
   `etc/config.yaml` is the default configuration file that images and packages load.
4. `deployment/values.yaml` and `deployment/templates/` define Helm behavior.
5. Tests under `internal/pkg/`, `tests/static`, `tests/host`,
   `tests/container`, and `tests/k8s` define executable contracts.
6. `README.md`, `deployment/README.md`, and test READMEs document
   repository-specific workflows and prerequisites. Keep the root README thin
   and link to the official guide for full user documentation.

Before handing off a metrics or deployment change, run the lowest applicable
checks:

- `go test ./internal/pkg/counters`
- `task test:static`
- `task test:unit`
- `task lint`
- `task fmt:check`
- `task validate`
- `task deps:sync:check` when version-derived artifacts change
- `task generate` when generated mocks or `go:generate` inputs change
- `task test:host` when host GPU/DCGM prerequisites exist
- `task build:e2e`, then `task test:e2e:smoke` (no GPU), `task test:e2e:host`
  (GPU and DCGM) or `task test:e2e:mocks` (root, a DCGM development build with
  NVML injection, `nv-hostengine` and `dcgmi`, and fixtures matching
  `DCGM_VERSION` in `NVML_INJECTION_DIR` and `NVSDM_MOCK_DIR`)
- `task build:image:local` and `task build:image:verify` when image labels or
  contents change
- `task test:container` when Docker and GPU prerequisites exist
- `task test:k8s` when a suitable Kubernetes cluster exists
- `task test:e2e` when the complete Docker, Kubernetes, DCGM, and GPU toolchain
  is available

Document GPU, Docker, Kubernetes, or DCGM prerequisites that prevent a gate from
running. Do not report skipped hardware-backed gates as passing.

## Metric CSV Authoring

Metric CSV rows have exactly three fields:

```text
DCGM FIELD, Prometheus metric type, help message
```

Rules:

- Lines beginning with `#` are comments.
- Active metric fields begin with `DCGM_` or `dcgm_`.
- Use a DCGM field that the current go-dcgm/DCGM bindings know, or one of the
  exporter-owned counters listed below.
- Supported scalar metric types are `counter`, `gauge`, and `untyped`.
- `label` rows are static label sources and are not rendered as standalone
  scalar metric families.
- On MIG GPUs with MIG instances selected, fields that DCGM declares at GPU
  level (for example power, temperature, clocks, utilization, and the PCIe,
  NVLink, and cycle-count profiling fields) are watched and read on the
  physical GPU and reported once per GPU, without `GPU_I_ID`, `GPU_I_PROFILE`,
  or `GPU_CI_ID` labels. These series carry no pod, container, or HPC job
  labels from the GPU's MIG instances; a pod or job that owns the whole GPU
  still gets them. GPU-level `label` fields still appear on instance series,
  with the physical GPU's value.
- Custom metrics supplied through Helm `config.metrics[].fields`, the deprecated
  Helm `customMetrics`, or mounted files are
  complete replacements for the default list, not additive overlays.
- Keep HELP text stable and clear; Prometheus families with the same name must
  not have conflicting HELP or TYPE metadata.
- Do not emit non-finite values or negative counter values.
- The exporter does not force a DCGM refresh when it starts watching fields.
  Fields that a DCGM module updates, such as profiling, NVSwitch and CPU
  fields, appear once the module first reports them, so early scrapes after a
  start or reload can lack them.

Exporter-owned counters:

- `DCGM_EXP_CLOCK_EVENTS_COUNT`
- `DCGM_EXP_XID_ERRORS_COUNT`
- `DCGM_EXP_GPU_HEALTH_STATUS`
- `DCGM_EXP_SYSTEM_HEALTH_STATUS`
- `DCGM_EXP_P2P_STATUS`
- `DCGM_EXP_XID_ERRORS_TOTAL`
- `DCGM_EXP_CLOCK_EVENTS_TOTAL`

Every `DCGM_EXP_GPU_HEALTH_STATUS` sample includes `health_watch`,
`health_error_code`, `health_error_severity`, and `health_error_category`
labels. PASS samples use `NONE` for severity and category; unrecognized DCGM
metadata uses `UNKNOWN`. GPU DRIVER recovery error 142 uses
`health_error_code="DCGM_FR_GPU_RECOVERY_IMEX_DOMAIN"`, not
`DCGM_FR_UNKNOWN(142)`; alert rules that match `DCGM_FR_UNKNOWN(142)` must
use this symbolic name instead.
A failing sample has value `20` (`DCGM_HEALTH_RESULT_FAIL`) and keeps its GPU
attribution and `health_error_severity`/`health_error_category` labels.

`DCGM_EXP_SYSTEM_HEALTH_STATUS` is opt-in and reports DCGM's host-level
health, as opposed to the per-GPU `DCGM_EXP_GPU_HEALTH_STATUS`. Today the only
host-level health watch DCGM has is IMEX, so the metric reports IMEX only and
emits one series with `health_watch="IMEX"`. A host-level watch DCGM adds later
would appear as another `health_watch` value on this metric, not as a new
metric. The series has no GPU or other device labels. Its only labels are `hostname`,
`health_watch`, `health_error_code`, `health_error_severity`, and
`health_error_category`; it has no workload, MIG, link, switch, or CPU identity
labels either. When DCGM reports no host-level IMEX incident, including when IMEX data
is missing or not watched, the series reports PASS (value `0`) with
`health_error_code="DCGM_FR_OK"` and `NONE` severity and category. If this
metric is configured and the DCGM hostengine does not support the IMEX health
watch, the exporter fails to start. DCGM reports its supported health watches
only from DCGM 4.7.1, so on DCGM 4.7.0 the exporter cannot confirm IMEX support
and fails to start when this metric is configured.

The `_COUNT` counters describe sampled observations during the configured
window, not unique events or state transitions. `DCGM_EXP_XID_ERRORS_COUNT`
counts sampled XID observations, including samples whose value is `0`.
`DCGM_EXP_CLOCK_EVENTS_COUNT` counts samples in which each reason is active.
The `_TOTAL` counters are in-memory cumulative totals intended for Prometheus
counter functions such as `increase()` and `rate()`.
`DCGM_EXP_XID_ERRORS_TOTAL` excludes XID value `0`.
`DCGM_EXP_CLOCK_EVENTS_TOTAL` increments on an inactive-to-active transition.
Publishing replacement collectors resets both totals to empty, and their
series are absent until a new event is counted. A configuration reload that
fails before replacement keeps the current collectors and their totals. Once
replacement collectors are published, or GPU lifecycle recovery clears the
registry, the old totals are no longer available even if retirement or
recovery subsequently fails.
A new `_TOTAL` series first appears with every event counted before its first
scrape, so `increase()` and `rate()` do not include those events. For alerts
that must see every XID, use `DCGM_EXP_XID_ERRORS_COUNT{xid!="0"} > 0`.
If reload, runtime swap, hot reload, or process restart behavior changes,
document whether cumulative state is reset or preserved and add tests.

The XID exporter counters read selected GPUs and GPU instances, their compute
instances, and required parent GPUs. Clock-event counters read physical GPUs
only, including the parent GPUs of selected GPU instances. Compute-instance
samples include `GPU_I_ID` and `GPU_CI_ID`. Each entity's history is counted separately; summing scopes does
not count unique physical failures. The direct `DCGM_FI_DEV_XID_ERROR` gauge
does not need to be enabled for either XID exporter counter to collect samples.

## CLI, Environment, And Runtime

CLI and environment behavior comes from `pkg/cmd/app.go`; defaults and value
checks come from `internal/pkg/appconfig`. The `config show`, `explain` and
`validate` reports are built in `internal/pkg/configinspect`.

Important contracts:

- The default listen address is `:9400`.
- `--health-require-gpus` / `DCGM_EXPORTER_HEALTH_REQUIRE_GPUS` and config-v2
  `server.health_require_gpus` should stay opt-in (default off). When on,
  `/health` returns 503 while no collector is
  registered under `FE_GPU`, so a liveness probe on `/health` restarts an
  exporter that came up against a hostengine with no GPUs visible. A reload in
  progress takes precedence and still returns 200. Note the predicate counts
  FE_GPU collectors, so a counters file contributing no FE_GPU fields also
  reads as zero.
- The default collectors file is `/etc/dcgm-exporter/default-counters.csv`.
- Remote DCGM hostengine values support `<HOST>:<PORT>`,
  `tcp://<HOST>:<PORT>`, `unix:///<SOCKET_PATH>`,
  `vsock://<CID>:<PORT>`, and bracketed IPv6 host:port values such as
  `[::1]:5555`.
- TLS and basic auth use Prometheus exporter-toolkit through
  `--web-config-file`; do not invent a separate config format.
- `--enable-pprof` exposes `/debug/pprof/` on the metrics port, stays opt-in, and
  needs a web config file that turns on TLS or basic auth.
- `--log-format` supports the formats declared by the CLI.
- `sources.dcgm.cleanup_timeout` (`--dcgm-cleanup-timeout`,
  `DCGM_EXPORTER_DCGM_CLEANUP_TIMEOUT`, default `5m`) is how long the exporter
  waits for DCGM on reload or GPU reset recovery, at shutdown, after a failed
  collector build, and when the GPU bind/unbind watch starts or stops. When the
  timeout runs out, the exporter exits so it can restart with a clean DCGM
  session. The
  orchestrator's stop grace period (Kubernetes default 30s, the systemd stop
  timeout) can end a shutdown wait first.
- Startup validation should fail clearly when required DCGM or runtime
  prerequisites are missing, unless startup validation is explicitly disabled.

## Kubernetes And Helm

Helm `arguments` pass through to the exporter binary. Use only CLI flags that
exist in `pkg/cmd/app.go`.

Rules:

- Keep Helm values, templates, raw YAML, and README examples aligned.
- The chart takes exporter settings from its `config` value, a version 2 file
  with snake_case keys. Do not add a chart value that sets an exporter setting
  through an environment variable or flag; chart values with camelCase names
  configure only Kubernetes objects.
- The chart mounts its config files as directories under
  `/etc/dcgm-exporter/chart/` (`config/`, `metrics/default-counters.csv`,
  `web-config/web-config.yaml`), and TLS certificates at
  `/etc/dcgm-exporter/tls`, never with `subPath`. The config mount holds only
  the `configMap.key` file and the metrics mount only the `metrics` key, so other
  keys of a `configMap.existingName` ConfigMap stay out of the pod. In chart examples, point
  `config.metrics[].file` at `/etc/dcgm-exporter/chart/metrics/default-counters.csv`.
- `config.server.write_timeout` and the ServiceMonitor scrape timeout/interval
  should remain coherent.
- Kubernetes pod labels and pod UID labels are emitted only when the matching
  Kubernetes options are enabled and RBAC permits the required reads.
- DRA and virtual GPU behavior must be explicitly enabled and tested or
  documented as a prerequisite-dependent path.
- Pod label allowlist regex values filter which pod labels are included in
  metrics by their original Kubernetes keys. Pod labels require a non-empty
  allowlist; `.*` selects all labels.
- Prometheus pod label names are sanitized. When allowed keys normalize to the
  same name, the lexicographically first original key keeps that name; others
  receive `_conflictN` suffixes, skipping occupied names. Names are stable for
  unchanged keys; adding or removing colliding keys can change suffix assignments.
- Local GPU k3d validation requires Linux, NVIDIA driver, Docker, k3d,
  kubectl, Helm, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, and a usable GPU.

## HPC Job Mapping

HPC job labels come from the HPC job mapping directory configured by the CLI or
environment. Mapping files are named after GPU IDs or GPU/MIG identifiers, and
each line contains job IDs for that GPU or MIG instance. Each line is trimmed;
blank lines, lines holding only `0` (Slurm epilog scripts write `0` when a job
ends; Slurm job IDs start at 1), and repeated lines are ignored. Do not synthesize job
IDs or mapping files in examples unless the user provides them. For MIG
mappings, the filename suffix is the GPU instance ID exported as `GPU_I_ID`,
not the `Device N` ordinal shown by `nvidia-smi -L`. Only files named after
exported GPUs and MIG instances are opened; other files are ignored without a
warning. Mapping files must be single-link regular files, and neither they nor
the directory's final component may be symlinks, so a ConfigMap volume must be
copied into regular files first. `sources.hpc_jobs.max_file_bytes`,
`max_job_id_bytes` and `max_jobs_per_file` (defaults 65536, 256 and 64; flags
`--hpc-job-mapping-max-*`) bound each file; a file over a limit adds no job
labels and keeps the GPU's samples.
When Kubernetes pod-label and HPC job enrichment are both enabled, the mapping
job keeps the `hpc_job` label. A pod label with that sanitized name moves to
`pod_label_hpc_job`, using the existing `_conflictN` suffix convention if that
fallback is occupied. Unmapped GPU samples keep their pod-label name unchanged.

## Docker, Packages, And systemd

Docker images and packages are user-visible release artifacts.

- `docker/Dockerfile` defines the distroless runtime image behavior.
- `packaging/config-files/systemd/nvidia-dcgm-exporter.service` defines host
  systemd defaults.
- The package-managed systemd unit should not be edited in-place by users;
  docs should prefer systemd drop-ins.
- Release and CI scripts must preserve checksum/signature verification and
  should not mask verification failures with `|| true`.
- Version-derived files are updated through `hack/versions.env` plus
  `task deps:sync`, then checked with `task deps:sync:check`.
- Container and package releases pair a DCGM version with an exporter version.
  Treat mismatched pairs as untested and unsupported; recommend updating to the
  latest paired release first when troubleshooting.
